snippets.output: A positive QuantiFERON gold test indicates latent tuberculosis (TB).
Elevated liver enzymes can be a side effect of many medications, including medications used to treat tuberculosis, but elevated liver enzymes are not a contraindication for treatment.
In a 27-year-old man with a positive QuantiFERON gold test started on tuberculosis treatment, the treatment can usually be adjusted to minimize liver enzyme elevation.
Hyperuricemia is a high level of uric acid in the blood and can be a side effect of certain medications used to treat tuberculosis.
Rifampicin is a medication used to treat tuberculosis.
Hyperuricemia is not typically an indication to discontinue treatment.
Optic neuritis is inflammation of the optic nerve and can be a side effect of some medications used to treat tuberculosis.
Isoniazid is a medication used to treat TB.
Optic neuritis is a rare side effect of tuberculosis treatment.
Optic neuritis is not typically an indication to discontinue treatment in a 27-year-old man with a positive QuantiFERON gold test consistent with latent tuberculosis.
Peripheral neuropathy is a well-known side effect of isoniazid and can occur at any time during tuberculosis treatment.
If peripheral neuropathy occurs in a 27-year-old man with a positive QuantiFERON gold test who was started on tuberculosis treatment, the tuberculosis treatment is often discontinued.
Red body excretions are not a known side effect of tuberculosis treatment.

Peripheral neuropathy is the most likely indication to discontinue treatment in a 27-year-old man with fatigue, cough, 15-pound weight loss over 3 weeks, recent release from prison, intravenous drug use in prison, and a positive QuantiFERON gold test consistent with latent tuberculosis.
Peripheral neuropathy is associated with isoniazid.
